learning_outcomes.text: Participants know the most important concepts of imperative and object-oriented programming.
Participants can design and implement their own programs.
Participants can work with basic computer science concepts such as correctness, runtime, Boolean algebra, invariants, and abstract data types.
Participants can purposefully use simple data structures (arrays, dictionaries) and know standard algorithms for them, especially for sorting arrays.

syllabus_topics: Imperative programming (variables, control structures, functions and recursion, error handling, event handling)
Introduction to a series of computer science concepts (invariants, runtime analysis, sorting algorithms, representation of data in the computer, Boolean algebra)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam. The module's grade contributes 8/138 to the final degree grade.
